# The modules a program can import: lib/ and lang/viv/std. Written by
# `viv features --write-modules` from each module's header; do not edit.
# tests/features.rs fails when it is stale.

== lang/viv/std/builtins
title: Builtins written in Viv (lang/viv/src/stdlib.rs)
summary: Builtins written in Viv (lang/viv/src/stdlib.rs). A program that calls one of these names, and does not define it, gets the def added before any engine sees the program, so the interpreter, C and wasm run the same code.
defs: 7
names: fsum, hypot, copysign, viv__sorted_num, viv__unique_num, viv__del_num, viv__del_strs

== lang/viv/std/contracts
title: The Viv contract library: objective-level solve verbs backed by a sweep of strategies, ...
summary: The Viv contract library: objective-level solve verbs backed by a sweep of strategies, written entirely in Viv (compileable on both the interpreter and the C backend). The design: a contract names the OBJECTIVE, not a method; debug mode runs every applicable strategy and fails loudly on dissent (methodological fuzzing); release mode runs the auto-selected strategy only.
defs: 13
names: q_gauss, q_asimp, q_adaptive, q_romberg, sweep_spread, sweep, q_methods, integrate, r_bisect, r_illinois, r_safe, r_methods, find_root

== lib/balance
title: Balanced truncation, or which states a model can do without
summary: A state-space model `(A, B, C)` of order `n` can usually be replaced by one of order `r` much smaller than `n` whose input-output behavior is nearly the same. Which `r` states, though? Not a subset of the original ones: the right answer is almost never "drop state 7".
defs: 6
names: hankel_values, balred, system_error, balred_error_abs, balred_error, balance_test_system

== lib/basis/all

A program that knows its basis set uses that set's module (`import basis.pople631g`) and links one table.
defs: 0
names: 

== lib/basis/basis
title: A basis set as a table, the record every lib/basis module returns
summary: A Gaussian basis set is a list of shells for each element. A shell has an angular momentum `l` and a contraction: exponents `a_p` and coefficients `c_p`, the radial part `sum_p c_p exp(-a_p r^2)`. The modules in lib/basis (generated by tools/basis_tables.py from the Basis Set Exchange) each return one `Basis` record:
defs: 6
names: basis_rows, basis_of, basis_first, basis_count, basis_nao, basis_check

== lib/basis/named
title: A basis set by its name, as PySCF spells it
summary: `basis_named(name)` gives the `Basis` record (lib/basis/basis) of the basis set PySCF would load for `name`. The name is read by PySCF's rule (`pyscf.gto.basis._format_basis_name`): lower case, with `-`, `_` and spaces taken out, so "6-31G*", "6-31g*", "631g*" and "6-31Gs" are one set. Then the key is looked up in the aliases PySCF 2.5.0 has for the eight sets here:
defs: 3
names: basis_key, basis_module, basis_named

== lib/cas/parse
title: Reading an expression written as Viv text into the CAS
summary: `cas(text)` reads an expression in Viv's own syntax into the store (lib/cas/store): numbers, names, `+ - * / ^`, parentheses and calls of the heads the CAS knows. The precedence is Viv's: `^` binds tightest and to the right, so `-x^2` is $-(x^2)$ and `2^3^2` is $2^9$; then unary minus; then `*` and `/`; then `+` and `-`.
defs: 13
names: cas_digit, cas_letter, cas_lex, cas_peek, cas_peek_kind, cas_bump, cas_decimal, cas_p_sum, cas_p_term, cas_p_unary, cas_p_power, cas_p_atom, cas

== lib/cas/phrases
title: Phrases as the CAS's first client, each closed form a check
summary: A phrase asks for a quantity, not an algorithm: `integrate x^2 from 1 to 2` asks for $\int_1^2 x^2\,dx$, and Gauss-Legendre is one way to get it. When the CAS has the quantity in closed form, the phrase's number can be held to it. `viv check --phrases prog.viv` writes a program that calls the defs below, one per phrase, and runs it (lang/viv/src/cas_check.rs).
defs: 14
names: json_q, json_num, cas_report, cas_report_val, cas_judge, cas_check_integral, cas_ends, cas_check_root, cas_check_deriv, cas_check_value, cas_check_refused, cas_check_summary, cas_check_holds, cas_deriv_at

== lib/cas/rational
title: Exact rationals and arithmetic mod p, in doubles
summary: The coefficients of the computer algebra system (lib/cas) are exact rationals `p/q`: `q > 0`, `gcd(p, q) = 1`. They are doubles holding integers: this library predates Viv's `Int`, and Viv has no big integers yet (features 1 and 5). A double holds every integer up to $2^{53} = 9007199254740992$ exactly; every operation here checks that its result stays below that, and gives NaN when it would not.
defs: 23
names: rat_bad, rat_gcd, rat_imul, rat_iadd, rat_norm, rat_add, rat_sub, rat_mul, rat_div, rat_pow, rat_cmp, rat_isqrt, rat_iroot, rat_square_part, mp_red, mp_add, mp_sub, mp_mul, mp_pow, mp_inv, mp_rat, mp_next, mp_point

== lib/cas/show
title: Printing a CAS expression as Viv and as LaTeX
summary: An expression in the store (lib/cas/store) is printed in two steps. First it becomes a syntax tree of the shape Viv's parser builds: `a + b`, `a - b`, `a * b`, `a / b`, `-a`, `pow(a, b)` (written `a ^ b`), calls, names and numbers.
defs: 19
names: sx, sx_num, sx_neg, sx_product, sx_rat, sx_of, sx_power, sx_mul, cas_negative_term, sx_sum, v_at, sx_text, cas_text, t_paren, t_at, t_name, sx_letter, sx_tex, cas_tex

== lib/cas/store
title: The expression store of lib/cas, one node per distinct expression
summary: An expression is a number, the id of a node in one store. The store keeps one node per distinct `(kind, payload, children)`: making a node looks its key up in a map and returns the id already there, so two equal expressions have the same id and equality is `a == b`.
defs: 41
names: cas_name, cas_node, cas_kind, cas_nk, cas_kid, cas_kids, cas_np, cas_nq, cas_name_of, cas_size, cas_fail, cas_isfail, cas_num, cas_int, cas_sym, cas_isnum, cas_isint, cas_isvar, cas_base, cas_expo, cas_cmp, cas_cmp_shape, cas_sort_by, cas_coeff, ... (17 more)

== lib/hf/accelerate
title: Speeding up the SCF fixed point by DIIS, plain iteration and damping
summary: One SCF iteration maps a Fock matrix to a density (diagonalize, occupy) and the density back to a Fock matrix (J and K). Plain iteration applies that map until nothing changes. It converges when the map is a contraction near the solution, which is often slowly and sometimes not at all: the density can swing between two shapes forever.

== lib/hf/cart2sph
title: From Cartesian to spherical Gaussians, one shell at a time
summary: The integral kernels in this library work on Cartesian components: a d shell has six (xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz) and an f shell ten. Most basis sets are defined on spherical components instead: five d functions and seven f. The sixth Cartesian d combination, xx + yy + zz = r^2, is an s function in disguise, and a spherical basis leaves it out.

== lib/hf/hermite
title: Hermite tables for McMurchie-Davidson integrals, built bottom-up
summary: Every integral in Hartree-Fock over Gaussians goes through the same move. The product of two Cartesian Gaussians on centers A and B, exponents `a` and `b`, is a Gaussian on the point `P = (aA + bB)/p` with exponent `p = a + b`, times a polynomial. McMurchie and Davidson write that polynomial as a sum of Hermite Gaussians, which are derivatives of the plain Gaussian with respect to `P`:
defs: 12

== lib/hf/iv_boys
title: The Boys function, enclosed
summary: lib/hf/boys computes `F_n(x) = int_0^1 t^(2n) exp(-x t^2) dt` to about 1e-15 and is held against an mpmath table. This module computes intervals that are guaranteed to contain `F_n(x)`, using only the outward-rounded operations of lib/hf/interval and the libm assumption stated there (`exp` within 2 ulps). The integral enclosures of lib/hf/iv_ints call it once per primitive pair or quartet.

== lib/hf/iv_sweep
title: Sweeping point strategies against a guaranteed enclosure
summary: The sweep drivers of lib/hf/sweep compare strategies with each other: the consensus is the elementwise median, and the member farthest from it is blamed. That has two blind spots. == lib/hf/orthogonalize
title: Four ways to make the AO basis orthonormal
summary: Atomic orbitals on neighboring atoms overlap, so the Roothaan equations `F C = S C e` carry the overlap matrix `S`. Any `X` with `X^T S X = I` turns them into an ordinary symmetric eigenproblem: with `C = X C'`,
defs: 16

== lib/hf/os_onebody
title: Overlap, kinetic and nuclear attraction by the Obara-Saika recurrences
summary: This module computes the three one-electron matrices an SCF needs, `S`, `T` and `V`, over unit-normalized Cartesian Gaussians, by the recurrences of Obara and Saika (J. Chem. Phys. 84, 3963, 1986). It is the second of the library's one-electron families.
defs: 14
names: os_ncum, os_cidx, os_ctab, os_s1d, os_t1d, os_st_block, os_overlap_block, os_kinetic_block, os_nuclear_block, os_hrr_pair, os_matrix, os_overlap, os_kinetic, os_nuclear

== lib/hf/rhf
title: Restricted Hartree-Fock, one set of orbitals with two electrons in each
summary: For a closed shell, with as many alpha as beta electrons, RHF puts both spins in the same orbitals. The state is one total density `D = 2 C_occ C_occ^T` (PySCF's `make_rdm1`), the Fock matrix is `F = H + J - K/2` and the energy `E = E_nuc + (1/2) Tr D (H + F)`.
defs: 7
names: rhf_t_water_setup, rhf_t_water, rhf_t_presets, rhf_t_all_presets, rhf_t_energy, rhf_t_stretched, rhf_t_import

== lib/hf/rohf
title: Restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock
summary: ROHF keeps one set of spatial orbitals for both spins: `Nb` closed-shell orbitals holding an alpha and a beta electron, `Na - Nb` open orbitals holding one alpha electron each, and the virtual rest. Unlike UHF the wavefunction is an eigenfunction of `S^2`, with `<S^2> = S(S+1)` exactly.
defs: 5
names: rohf_t_options, rohf_t_water, rohf_t_pair, rohf_t_import, rohf_t_regime

== lib/hf/rys_eri
title: Electron repulsion integrals by Rys quadrature
summary: This is the third ERI algorithm in lib/hf, next to McMurchie-Davidson and Head-Gordon-Pople. It shares no code with either: it never builds Hermite expansions or Obara-Saika intermediates, and it does not call the Boys function. Its tests use Boys as the oracle for the quadrature rule.
defs: 14
names: rys_applicable, rys_nroot, rys_gl_half, rys_work_new, rys_hypot, rys_tql, rys_roots, rys_binom, rys_shell_quartet, rys_eri, rys_rng, rys_moment_gap, rys_moment_worst, rys_rule_ok

== lib/hf/scf_loop
title: The SCF loop every Hartree-Fock method runs
summary: Hartree-Fock replaces the electron-electron repulsion by the average field of the other electrons. That field depends on the orbitals, and the orbitals depend on the field, so the equations are solved by iteration: guess a density, build the Fock matrix from it, diagonalize, occupy the lowest orbitals, and repeat until the density stops changing.
defs: 27
names: scf_setup, scf_setup_with, scf_method, scf_opts, scf_weight, scf_nocc, scf_incremental, scf_nmatrix, scf_swapped, scf_energy2, scf_commutator, scf_level_shift, scf_diagonalize, scf_occupy, scf_iterate, scf_coefficients, scf_aufbau, scf_orbitals, scf_result, scf_unswap, scf_solve, scf, scf_run_from, scf_step, ... (3 more)

== lib/hf/stab
title: Is an SCF solution a minimum? Orbital-rotation stability
summary: An SCF run stops where the density commutes with its own Fock matrix. That condition says the energy is stationary: no small rotation of an occupied orbital into a virtual one changes E to first order. It does not say E goes up in every direction.
defs: 28
names: stab_orbitals, stab_split, stab_nparam, stab_density, stab_fock_mo, stab_mo_eri, stab_fill_block, stab_layout, stab_hess_mo, stab_hop, stab_hess_jk, stab_hess_methods, stab_hessian, stab_gradient, stab_expm, stab_rotate, stab_energy_d, stab_energy, stab_energy_along, stab_curvature, stab_slope, stab_quad, stab_lowest, stab_label, ... (4 more)

== lib/lobpcg
title: LOBPCG, the lowest eigenpairs of an operator you can only apply
summary: `lobpcg(apply_h, precondition, vectors, values, max_steps, nconv, tol)` finds the lowest few eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a Hermitian operator `H` that is given as a function: `apply_h(x)` returns `H` applied to each row of `x`. The matrix is never formed, so `H` can be a stencil, an FFT sandwich, or anything else that is cheaper to apply than to store.
defs: 20
names: row_length, row_norms, divide_rows, stacked, rayleigh_quotients, residuals, largest_of_first, no_preconditioner, orthonormalizer, lowest_ritz_coefficients, search_directions, lobpcg_start, lobpcg_step, lobpcg, apply_laplacian_1d, apply_laplacian_2d, unstructured_matrix, apply_unstructured, random_rows, worst_eigen_residual

== lib/lqr
title: The linear-quadratic regulator, for a system with one input
summary: Given a linear system `zdot = A z + B u` and a price on being away from zero and on pushing, `W` and `r`, the gains that minimize the total bill are `K = B^T P / r`, where `P` solves the algebraic Riccati equation
defs: 7
names: lqr_riccati, lqr_riccati_step, lqr_riccati_integrated, lqr_residual, lqr_gains, lqr_closed_loop, lqr_slowest

== lib/minpack/fit

== lib/minpack/lmder
title: MINPACK's lmder, Levenberg-Marquardt least squares with a trust region
summary: A port of `lmder.f` and `lmder1.f` from netlib MINPACK (lib/minpack/ref), with the Fortran's arithmetic in the Fortran's order, so that the iterates match a gfortran build of the original to the last bit where the problem's own functions do. The explanation is in lib/minpack/lmder.intent; the checks are in lib/minpack/mgh_check.viv and lib/minpack/check.sh.
defs: 5
names: lmder, lmder1_maxfev, lmder1, lm_rosenbrock, lm_rosenbrock_oracle

== lib/minpack/mgh
title: Test problems for least squares, from Moré, Garbow and Hillstrom
summary: Eleven of the eighteen problems of MINPACK's own test driver for lmder (`ref/file17.f`: SSQFCN, SSQJAC and INITPT), ported with the Fortran's arithmetic in its order, so the Viv port of lmder can be compared with a gfortran build of the original iterate by iterate. The problems are those of Moré, Garbow and Hillstrom, "Testing Unconstrained Optimization Software", ACM TOMS 7 (1981) 17-41.

== lib/nn_adjoints
title: The backward passes of lib/nn, written by hand
summary: Before Viv had `value_and_grad`, each piece of `lib/nn` came with a backward pass written by hand: given the gradient of the loss with respect to the piece's output, the gradients with respect to its inputs and weights. Model code no longer uses them; `value_and_grad` generates the same gradients from the forward pass. They are kept here as references.

== lib/nprandom/pcg64
title: NumPy's PCG64 in 16-bit limbs
summary: `np.random.default_rng(seed)` is a `Generator` over PCG64: a 128-bit linear congruential state, `state = state * MULT + inc mod 2^128`, and a 64-bit output, the high and low halves of the new state XORed and rotated right by the state's top six bits (XSL-RR).
defs: 8
names: npr_pcg_new, npr_pcg_step, npr_pcg_next64, npr_pcg_next32, npr_pcg_double, npr_word64, npr_pcg_seed, npr_pcg_from_entropy

== lib/nprandom/seedseq
title: NumPy's SeedSequence, the hash behind default_rng(seed)
summary: `np.random.default_rng(seed)` does not use the seed as the state. It hands the seed to `SeedSequence`, which hashes its 32-bit words into a pool of four words and draws the generator's initial state from the pool.
defs: 5
names: npr_ss_words, npr_ss_hashmix, npr_ss_mix, npr_ss_pool, npr_ss_generate

== lib/nuclear/shell/shell
title: The nuclear shell model in the M scheme
summary: A configuration-interaction (shell-model) code. It reads a single-particle space (a `.sps` file) and an isospin two-body interaction (a `.int` file), builds every Slater determinant of Z valence protons and N valence neutrons with total angular-momentum projection M, and applies the Hamiltonian to a vector (`apply_h`); lib/eigen/lowest finds its lowest eigenstates.
defs: 22
names: data_lines, read_space, exchange_phase, vjt_index, put_vjt, factorial, clebsch, mscheme_tables, popcounts, below, make_species, group_of, make_basis, species_h, species_jumps, apply_h_into, apply_h, j_squared, j_from_j2, occupations, mass_scale, lowest_m2

== lib/ode/dopri5
title: Dormand and Prince's explicit 5(4) pair
summary: Seven stages give a fifth-order solution and an embedded fourth-order one; their difference estimates the local error, and the step is accepted when that error, weighted by atol + rtol |y|, has RMS norm below 1. The seventh stage is evaluated at the new point, so it is the next step's first stage ("first same as last"): six evaluations per step.
defs: 1
names: dopri_step

== lib/ode/lu
title: Dense LU with partial pivoting, factored once and solved many times
summary: The implicit integrators (lib/ode/radau.viv, lib/ode/bdf.viv) solve with the same Newton matrix for several iterations and often for several steps, so the factorization is kept: `lu_factor` overwrites a copy of the matrix with its L and U factors and records the row swaps; `lu_solve` then costs n^2 per right-hand side instead of n^3.

== lib/ode/problems

== lib/polar
title: Orthogonalizing a matrix by Newton-Schulz, which is what Muon does
summary: Every real matrix factors as `A = U H` with `U` orthonormal and `H` symmetric positive semidefinite. `U` is the polar factor, and it is the closest orthonormal matrix to `A` in the Frobenius norm. Robotics wants it because a rotation matrix integrated forward stops being a rotation, and the polar factor is how you put it back.
defs: 11
names: frob, ns_poly, ns_step, ns_normalize, newton_schulz, polar_factor, muon_direction, polar_h, singular_values, row_orthonormality, polar_test_matrix

== lib/randla/dense

== lib/randla/lowrank
title: Randomized low-rank approximation by range finder, SVD, Nystrom and RPCholesky
summary: The idea of Halko, Martinsson and Tropp (SIAM Review 53, 2011): multiply A by a random matrix with a few more columns than the rank you want, and the product's columns span nearly all of A's dominant range. Everything after that is deterministic linear algebra on matrices with k columns.
defs: 9
names: range_finder, qb, rsvd, nystrom_fn, nystrom, rpcholesky_fn, rpcholesky, with_spectrum, poly_decay

== lib/randla/sketch
title: Sketching operators, generated from a counter
summary: A sketching operator S is a random matrix with far fewer rows than columns (or the reverse) that keeps the geometry of the vectors it is applied to: for every x in a fixed subspace of dimension n, |Sx| stays within a factor 1 +- eps of |x| once S has a small multiple of n rows. Every algorithm in randla starts by applying one.
defs: 9
names: gaussian, rademacher, saso_nonzeros, saso_apply, saso_dense, next_pow2, fwht_rows, sample_rows, srht_apply

== lib/randla/trace
title: Trace estimation from matrix-vector products by Hutchinson and Hutch++
summary: Both estimators see the matrix only through `apply(X)`, which returns A X for an n-by-s block X: a def or a lambda, so A can be an operator never stored (a Hessian, a matrix function applied by Lanczos, an inverse applied by a solver).
defs: 4
names: hutchinson_fn, hutchpp_fn, hutchinson, hutchpp

== lib/randlc
title: randlc, the NAS Parallel Benchmarks' random number generator
summary: The NAS Parallel Benchmarks draw every random number from one linear congruential generator: `x_{k+1} = a * x_k mod 2^46`, returned as the uniform `2^-46 * x_{k+1}` in (0, 1). The seeds and multipliers in the benchmarks (`a = 5^13 = 1220703125`, `s = 271828183` for EP and IS, `314159265` for CG) are odd integers below 2^46.
defs: 3
names: randlc, vranlc, randlc_split

== lib/random
title: Random draws, each one a formula over rand()
summary: Viv's `rand()` is Park-Miller MINSTD: `srand(seed)` sets the state to `floor(|seed|) mod 2147483646 + 1`, and each `rand()` moves it to `16807 * state mod 2147483647` and returns `state / 2147483647`, a number in (0, 1).
defs: 7
names: randn, randn_matrix, randint, arange, shuffle, randperm, choice

== lib/scf/loop
title: One self-consistent field loop for any basis
summary: `scf` runs a self-consistent field: from densities, the mean fields; from the fields, the single-particle Hamiltonian of every block; each block's lowest eigenpairs, filled with particles by energy; from the occupied states, new densities; the next densities by mixing the old and the new; and again, until the energy changes by less than `e_tol` between passes.
defs: 1
names: scf

== lib/scf/mix
title: Mixing densities in a self-consistent field
summary: `mix_densities(x_in, x_out, hist)` is a contract: the density the next pass of a self-consistent field starts from, made from the density the pass started with (`x_in`), the one it produced (`x_out`) and the earlier pairs in `hist`. The densities are one flat array; a solver packs whatever it mixes (lib/skyrme packs rho, tau and J of both kinds).
defs: 12
names: mix_start, remember, residual_norm, linear, pulay, broyden, mix_densities, probe_map, by_linear, by_pulay, by_broyden, probe_solve

== lib/stats
title: The mean and the standard deviation of an array

== lib/stats/glm

summary: `glm_irls(y, X, w, offset, family, link, ...)` is R's glm.fit step for step: the same starting means, the same working response and weights, each weighted least-squares step by lib/stats/linmod.viv's pivoted QR (R's tolerance min(1e-7, epsilon / 1000)), the same clamps in the link functions (logit at |eta| = 30, probit at Phi^-1(eps), the log link's mean at least eps), and R's stopping rule |dev -...
defs: 14
names: linkfun, linkinv, mu_eta, variance, ylogy, unit_deviance, deviance, mustart, glm_irls, neg_score_slope, score, observed_info, glm_observed_cov, glm_newton

== lib/stats/linmod
title: Least squares for linear models and GLMs
summary: The least-squares solver slot of vp.stats. Every solver takes the design X (n by p) and y and returns the coefficients, the rank, the columns used, and (X^T X)^-1 over those columns (NaN rows and columns for the others):
defs: 15
names: col_scale, exact_residual, swap_columns, qr_pivot, apply_qt, apply_q, exact_xtr, forward_solve_rt, back_solve, cov_from_r, lstsq_qr, lstsq_chol, cho_solve, lstsq_svd, lstsq

== lib/stats/special
title: The special functions under lib/stats's distributions
summary: Each function takes and returns one number. The methods, and where each is held to mpmath at 50 digits, are in lib/stats/accuracy.py (the grid) and lib/stats/accuracy.json (the worst errors found, beside SciPy's and R's).

names: log1p, expm1, log1pmx, exp_mhalfsq, zeta_series, lgamma1p_small, lgamma2p_small, stirling_series, lgamma, lgamma1p, digamma, psi_zeta_series, stirl_step, stirlerr, bd0, dpois_raw, dbinom_raw, erf_series, stats_erf, erfcx, exp_msq, exp_msq_split, erfc, ndtr, ... (26 more)

== lib/svd
title: The singular value decomposition, by one-sided Jacobi
summary: `A = U S V^T`, with `U` and `V` orthonormal and `S` diagonal and non-negative. This is the decomposition that answers what a matrix does to the unit sphere, what its rank is when the answer is not a whole number, and which directions of its input it barely notices.
defs: 5
names: svd_jacobi, svd, svd_residual, svd_orthonormal, svd_with_values

== lib/xyz
title: Atoms from XYZ text
summary: `parse_xyz(text)` reads a molecule's atoms into a `Geometry`: each atom's symbol, its atomic number, and the positions as an n x 3 array, in the text's unit (angstroms, in an XYZ file). lib/hf/mole builds a Hartree-Fock `Molecule` from the same text.
defs: 2
names: atomic_number, parse_xyz
